ORBIS needs this to tell which screen you are on inside an app — for example Instagram Reels versus Instagram Stories. Only Reels, Shorts and Spotlight are ever slowed; Stories, messages and normal videos are left alone. ORBIS reads screens only in the apps it targets, keeps everything on your device, and never sends anything anywhere.
Let ORBIS see your screen time

It needs to know how long you spend in Instagram, YouTube, Snapchat and WhatsApp. Android only lets you allow this from Settings — the button opens the right list, then find ORBIS in it and switch it on.
Let ORBIS tell Reels from your chats
This is what reads which screen is open. Without it nothing can be slowed. Settings → Accessibility → Downloaded apps → ORBIS surface detection.

1. It spots reels — it knows Reels from your chats.

2. It slows them in bursts — every few seconds the feed is squeezed for a moment, then let go. Enough to break the spell, never enough to break the app.

3. You earn it back — fifteen minutes away from the feed buys five minutes at full speed.

Slowed a little: Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts, Snapchat Spotlight, and those same feeds opened in a browser.\n\nNever touched: WhatsApp — all of it, always. DMs, chats and calls in any app. Instagram Stories and your normal feed. Normal-length YouTube videos. Games, school work, and every other app on your phone.

What ORBIS can see right now
Open Instagram, YouTube or Snapchat and this will fill in.
On while one of those feeds is on screen, off a few seconds after you leave it.
The test slows every app ORBIS covers for 30 seconds, then stops on its own. It is for checking ORBIS works, not for everyday use — the switch above does that.
Nothing is being slowed. Everything is at full speed.

ORBIS makes endless-scroll video feeds load slightly slower, so the scroll that was going to swallow an hour gets interrupted by you noticing it.\n\nIt only ever slows Reels, Shorts and Spotlight. It never slows WhatsApp, your DMs, your Stories or anything else. Everything it knows about you stays on this phone.
What gets slowed, and what never does
WhatsApp is never slowed. Not any part of it.

WhatsApp is how you talk to people, not something you scroll at, so it is excluded at the deepest level ORBIS has: while the slow-down is active, WhatsApp\'s traffic is not routed through ORBIS at all. It is not a setting that could be flipped by accident — the phone\'s own network layer enforces it.
What ORBIS can see about you

Everything stays on this phone. There is no ORBIS account, no server, no cloud backup and no sync. Nothing is uploaded anywhere, because there is nowhere for it to be uploaded to.

Stored: how many minutes a day you spent in the four tracked apps, which of those screens you are on right now (in memory only), and the clear time you earned and spent each day.

Never seen: what you post, type, send or read. Who you talk to. Any screen in any app other than the four it tracks.

1. Detection spots the feed. ORBIS checks which app is in front and which of its screens is showing. In a browser it reads the address bar instead.

2. The local VPN comes up — only then, and only for the one app you are scrolling. Every other app, WhatsApp included, is left off it entirely.

3. The feed is squeezed, then let go. Every few seconds the app's downloads are held to a trickle for a moment, then released. Videos stall, recover, and stall again — and that stutter is exactly the moment you notice you have been scrolling.

4. It comes back down. Leave the feed and the VPN drops within a few seconds.

Detection relies on recognising specific parts of Instagram, YouTube and Snapchat\'s screens. When those apps get redesigned — and they do — ORBIS can stop recognising a feed until it is updated. The failure is a safe one: it stops slowing things, it never starts slowing the wrong thing.\n\nYou are never locked in. The Controls tab has one switch that stops the slow-down completely, and every permission can be revoked in Android\'s own Settings at any time.
ORBIS %1$s · everything on this page happens on this phone and nowhere else
